note: Port fidelity (port_fidelity.py): each difference between the Swift pipeline and facts.py on the same answers, investigated, with the rule that makes Swift decide differently on purpose. Keyed '<set> <mode> <story>#<order> <item>' (or 'h2 time-model - <question>'), with the exact value on each side: an entry excuses only that difference, and one that no longer occurs fails the gate. Phase 13a.2 Gates step. accepted_points: aggregate differences over 1 point the author accepted (each with its reason and who accepted it); the author accepted the four of the Gates step's preparation on 19 November 2026; two follow from the fix round they asked for.

rules.alias: §11.4 alias trust: a trusted memory's roster leaves out people named so far only in untrusted memories, so the trusted memories' person is another entity and the phrase has more holders (facts.py has no alias trust). Same person.
rules.untrusted_episode: §11.4: the only episode the link rests on has only untrusted evidence, so the basis is untrusted (facts.py says sole_known). Same person.
rules.untrusted_rules_out: §11.4/§11.9 trust: an untrusted memory never resolves a trusted memory's phrase nor rules a holder out ('only trusted evidence does either'), so an earlier reference stays undecided where facts.py used an agent's note. A miss, never a wrong link.
rules.label: §11.4 labels: a fact's label is the latest trusted statement's (facts.py keeps the first), which changes the phrase's label class and so its holders or uniqueness. Same person.
rules.stale: 13a.1: a decision is invalidated when its holders change, and the re-read's answer replaces it (facts.py kept its earlier group decision). Both are misses, not wrong links.
rules.quote: 13a.1 language layer, failing closed: a role phrase that may be quoted speech is skipped (facts.py linked it to someone else, also not a link to a person).
rules.intent: §11.7: the timeline intent grammar fails closed (narrowed after 13a.1 round 17), so the question gets no intent: a miss, never a wrong answer.
rules.daycue: §11.4: a day preposition next to the phrase is a time cue ('my landlord on 9 June 2023'); facts.py doesn't read it and links the current holder, which the story forbids. Swift is right.
rules.schedule: When a phrase is sent to the reader and when code resolves it depends on the holders at reading time and on reconciliation's schedule (13a.2's queue); a stored decision keeps its basis (context) where code alone would say sole_known, in the other order for each pipeline. Same person.
rules.org_containment: §11.4 organizations: one name inside another ('Bracken', 'Bracken Systems') is a merge suggestion, never merged, so Swift keeps two entities whose episodes overlap and tells the answer; facts.py merges them by containment and answers. Never a wrong answer.
rules.lexicon_recording: 13a.2's fix round added 'supervisor', singular 'parent' and the class 'client contact' to both registries. The spike's recorded facts.py lines (results-h3b) predate them, so facts.py never detected these phrases there; the Swift replay of the same recorded answers detects them and resolves them in code (named, sole_known, or candidates when it can't tell). Never a wrong link. The mixed gold play, rerun through facts.py with the new registry, agrees with Swift exactly.
